 Is it curtains for COLA? Saving Social Security could mean changing the cost-of-living adjustment.
 Several proposals consider changing the way retirees receive inflation protection. Here’s what it could cost you.
 Updated Oct. 31, 2026, 2:33 p.m. ET Share Resize (10 min)
 Many Americans rely on the cost-of-living adjustment, but altering it might be one provision in a package to fix the program’s insolvency issue. Photo: MarketWatch photo illustration / iStockphoto For U.S. workers, Social Security is a cherished benefit. It’s guaranteed lifetime income that adjusts every year to keep up with inflation.
 That yearly cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA, is crucial because it allows older Americans to retain their purchasing power. But with Social Security facing insolvency in the next six years, the way in which recipients receive that perk may change substantially.
